assessment_summary: The author attempts an inductive proof but gets stuck in Case 2, so they switch to an algorithmic approach (lines 0039-0057). The algorithm is standard, but the proof of termination is fundamentally flawed. In step 0053, the author erroneously claims that the large component 'becomes the union of all other components plus v_i' (the component in the opposite direction). This completely ignores the subtrees of the large component that remain after moving. Step 0054 compounds this with an algebraic error, calculating the size of this component as n - |C| - 1 instead of n - |C|. Because the remaining pieces of the large component are never analyzed, the claim in step 0056 that the maximum component size strictly reduces is completely unsupported.
counterexample: Let T be the path A-B-C-D-E (n=5). Start at v_0=A. The only component of T-A is C = {B,C,D,E} with size 4 > 5/2. We move to v_1=B. Step 0053 claims that after moving, the large component C 'becomes the union of all other components plus v_i' (which here is just {A}). This is false: C does not become {A}; rather, C splits and its remaining vertices form the component {C,D,E} of T-B. By confusing the components, the proof ignores {C,D,E} (size 3). Furthermore, step 0054 calculates the size of the new component as n - |C| - 1 = 5 - 4 - 1 = 0, whereas {A} has size 1 and {C,D,E} has size 3. Because it ignores the pieces of C, the proof fails to justify that the maximum component size strictly reduces (step 0056).
